input:
The reboiler wall thickness is 52 mm, obtained once the corrosion allowance has been added to the pressure-retaining thickness. The figure represents the two components together: the allowance is not a separate plate or a later addition, and the combined figure of 52 mm is carried on the fabrication drawing. Over the service life, the allowance is consumed as the wall thins, so the thickness at any later inspection is the original 52 mm less the loss the allowance was intended to absorb. The allowance plays no part in increasing the pressure the shell can carry at the end of life, since the check at that stage is performed on the thinned wall, and the figure of 52 mm belongs to the as-new condition. The reboiler stands in the solvent circuit served by the lean solvent pump, and its flanged joints form part of that circuit.

Two candidate gasket materials are assessed against one another purely in terms of temperature limit. Other criteria, including pressure class, seating stress and resistance to the solvent, do not form the grounds of the comparison, because the two materials could not be separated on those grounds in the data available to this section. On temperature limit, by contrast, the two materials separate clearly. One material is rated for continuous service above the highest temperature the reboiler reaches in service, whereas the other reaches its rating limit within the temperatures the reboiler experiences. The higher-rated material is accordingly preferred, albeit on that single ground alone.

The preference is a limited one: it says nothing about which material seals better at low temperature, nothing about relative cost, and nothing about availability, none of which this section addresses. What it indicates is that, at a joint operating at elevated temperature, the lower-rated material works close to the boundary of its limit while the higher-rated material retains a margin, and the gasket at the edge of its temperature limit is the one most likely to relax and weep in service. The lower-rated material is not excluded from the unit as a whole: it remains a candidate at joints whose temperatures stay below its limit, and the comparison is at its sharpest at the reboiler flanges, where the joint temperature comes closest to the lower rating.
